topic: How do interference mitigation techniques adapt when handling tunneled versus non-tunneled traffic in multi-beam satellite systems?
consensus_response: Interference mitigation techniques in multi-beam satellite systems must adapt differently for tunneled versus non-tunneled traffic. For tunneled traffic, which experiences increased intrabeam interference due to frequency reuse, techniques like rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) and interference alignment may be required. AI and machine learning can optimize these techniques dynamically, balancing performance and complexity. For non-tunneled traffic, analog beamforming can be simpler but may not fully address intercell interference. A hybrid approach combining simpler and advanced techniques can provide a practical solution while maintaining performance.
